patch.objective: Use network security policies to restrict cluster-level access: default-deny NetworkPolicies per namespace and explicit allow rules for the few paths workloads need

sources.cite: CNCF CKS Curriculum v1.37 (cncf/curriculum, pinned commit 0a8cc08a): Cluster Setup 15%, Cluster Hardening 15%, System Hardening 10%, Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities 20%, Supply Chain Security 20%, Monitoring, Logging and Runtime Security 20%
sources.note: The curriculum was read in primary text on 2026-11-07 by the course builder (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/kubernetes.ts). On 2026-11-17 a third-party summary (slauger.github.io/kubestronaut/cks/monitoring-logging-runtime) confirmed the 20% domain; the PDF itself was not re-read. The objective wording is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's falco-shell-in-catalog-pod (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.
Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the page found by search (as in the base case): a rule selecting an endpoint with an egress section makes that direction default-deny.

The company, the cluster, the services and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.
